Good web design in Seattle has a tougher audience than most places. The person reading your page on the bus may spend the workday building apps, testing interfaces or measuring load times, and they notice when a site stutters, jumps around while it loads, or hides the phone number three menus deep. They will not write you a complaint. They will just open the next result.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson, who writes and builds every page himself. You see a free demo of your site first. The prices are printed: $497, $997 or $1,997, paid once.

Seattle web design for a city full of people who build the web

This is not a guess about the local crowd. In CBRE's 2026 tech talent ranking, the Seattle area held second place, and tech jobs made up 10.2% of all employment in the metro, close to double the 5.5% average across the 50 markets CBRE studied. That is a lot of customers who know what a well made page feels like.

You do not need animation or a clever layout to impress them. You need the basics done properly: a page that appears quickly on a phone signal, text big enough to read, buttons that are easy to hit, and nothing that shifts under a thumb. A coffee counter in Fremont, a tile installer working out of Georgetown and a tutoring service near the U District all get judged by the same yardstick.

Six things a picky visitor tests in the first ten seconds

Nobody runs this list on purpose. They just leave when something on it fails. Here is how each point is handled on a site Maurice builds.

  • SpeedPages are kept light: photos sized for the screen they show on and no pile of add-ons, so the site opens quickly even on a weak signal.
  • A stable layoutPhotos have set sizes, so text does not jump as the page loads and nobody taps the wrong link.
  • Readable on any screenBody text is a comfortable size with strong contrast, on phones, tablets and desktops.
  • Usable without a mouseClear headings, real link text and alt text on images, so people using a keyboard or a screen reader can still find their way.
  • Plain wordsWhat you do, where, and what happens next, written the way you would say it at the counter. No filler about passion and synergy.
  • A contact form that worksEvery submission lands in your email, and the phone number dials with one tap from the top of each page.

Web design in Seattle, Washington, one neighborhood at a time

Seattle people say where they live by neighborhood, not by city. Ballard, Fremont, Capitol Hill, Columbia City, the U District and Georgetown each have their own main streets and their own regulars, and a business that names its part of town reads as local to the people nearby. Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence: how well your business matches a search, how far it is from the searcher or the place they named, and how well known it is. Saying clearly where you are helps with the first two.

West Seattle shows how strong that identity is. People search for "west seattle web design" on its own, and the neighborhood has its own downtown. The West Seattle Junction grew up where two streetcar lines met at California Avenue SW and SW Alaska Street in 1907, and by the end of that decade it had taken over from the Admiral district as the area's commercial center. Today its merchants work together through the West Seattle Junction Association. A shop on California Avenue gains little from a page that only says "Seattle."

East of Lake Washington the same logic applies. Bellevue, Redmond and Kirkland are separate cities with their own searches. If your crew crosses the bridge every day, say so in plain words and give those cities their own pages. If you never go there, say that too, so nobody calls for a job you will turn down.

When every hour of payroll costs more

Seattle's minimum wage went to $21.30 an hour on January 1, 2026, up from $20.76 in 2025, and the city's Office of Labor Standards applies the same rate to small employers as to large ones. For a five-person shop, time spent answering the same question by phone all day adds up fast.

A good site takes some of that load. A clear page on what you do and do not do saves the calls that end with "sorry, we do not do that." A plain list of service areas stops the out-of-range requests. A short FAQ answers parking, deposits and lead times before anyone picks up the phone. And a quote form that asks the right questions up front means the first call back is a useful one.

For trades that cover a wide area, such as cleaners, plumbers or electricians, the service area page is where that saving shows up first. It tells a caller in Lake City or Rainier Beach whether you come to them before they spend your time asking.

Website design in Seattle without the agency overhead

Some owners search for a "web development agency Seattle" when what they want is a solid small business site. A development agency is the right call for custom software, a member portal or an app. We do not build those, and an online store with a cart is not part of our packages either. What we do build is a hand-written site that explains your business and turns visitors into calls and quote requests.

We do not sell page counts. Fifteen useful pages about Ballard and your actual services do more than fifty thin ones. A fuller explanation is on our pricing page.

One piece of local paperwork belongs on your launch list too. The City of Seattle says most businesses operating in the city need a business license tax certificate, renewed every year. Have it sorted before your address goes up on a new site.

Free and low-cost help for Seattle owners

Seattle Office of Economic Development

The city runs an Accounting and Business Consulting program with up to 10 hours of free one-on-one help per topic for eligible Seattle small businesses and nonprofits, covering areas from bookkeeping to marketing. It also offers free legal counseling and workshops on topics such as commercial leases.

Washington Small Business Development Center

A statewide network of more than 30 business advisors, run by Washington State University with the U.S. Small Business Administration. Advising is one-on-one and costs nothing.

Seattle Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce

Its 2026 membership prospectus reports about 2,500 member companies, 80% of them small to mid-size, and the chamber runs a Small Business Advisory Group that gives input on its programs and policy work.

Your neighborhood business association

Groups like the West Seattle Junction Association run events and shared services for their merchants. They are worth a call, and a listing in their directory is one more way for neighbors to find you.

Common questions

Who does Seattle web design without a monthly agency retainer?

We do. The build is one payment: Starter is $497, Pro is $997 and Agency is $1,997. You own the finished site. The only recurring items are hosting, maintenance and updates at $49 a month, which are included while you keep an AI agent, and the AI chat widget or phone agent at $297 a month if you keep one after its free trial. The phone agent can be canceled any time.

Do you build WordPress sites for Seattle businesses?

We do not promise a particular platform. Maurice builds each site by hand and you own the result. If you need WordPress or another system for a reason, for example a staff member who already edits it, say so when you ask for the free demo and he will tell you plainly whether that fits.

Can you build an ecommerce website for my Seattle shop?

Not inside our packages. An online store with a cart and checkout is not included in Starter, Pro or Agency, and we would rather tell you that now than after you pay. What we do build well is the site that brings people to your counter: what you carry, your hours, where you are, and how to call or ask for a quote.

Will you write a separate page for West Seattle or the Eastside?

If you serve those areas, yes. The Starter site has one service area page that names where you work. Pro adds ten city pages, each researched and written for one place, so a West Seattle page talks about West Seattle and a Bellevue page talks about Bellevue, rather than one paragraph with the name swapped.

Is website design in Seattle more expensive than in other cities?

Local firms carry Seattle wages and rents, and that can show up in their quotes. Our prices are the same everywhere because the work is done remotely from East Texas. Whatever you compare, ask each designer for the full first-year cost in writing, including hosting and any monthly add-ons.
